mainTopic: The three camps in שילה and refuge in מחנה לויה; which offerings were brought on private במות and at the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל
overview: A ברייתא taught that in שילה 'there were only two camps,' and the גמרא works out what this means. Removing מחנה לויה would put זבין and טמאי מתים outside the same single camp, against the Torah's plural 'their camps.' רבא shows that removing מחנה ישראל fails too, because זבין and מצורעים would then share one place, while a מצורע must dwell alone. So all three camps existed in שילה. 'Only two camps' means that מחנה לויה did not give refuge to an accidental killer there. A ברייתא proves that in the מדבר it did give refuge, and from this comes a rule: a לוי who kills by accident is exiled to another district, or even to another part of his own, based on 'כִּי בְעִיר מִקְלָטוֹ יֵשֵׁב.' The גמרא then turns to גלגל, where private במות were allowed. It brings a ברייתא in which רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about which offerings an individual could bring on a private במה. A second ברייתא gives three views on what was brought at the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל: רבי יהודה, חכמים, and רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון's list continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The plural 'camps' shows the Levite camp existed in שילה
steps.stepSummary: If מחנה לויה were missing in שילה, זבין and טמאי מתים would be sent out of the same single camp. The Torah's plural 'their camps' demands a separate camp for each group.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were no Levite camp, then זבין and people impure from a dead body would both be sent out of just one camp. But the Torah said 'that they not defile their camps,' which means: give one camp to this group and another camp to that group.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing an argument about which camp was missing in שילה. It proves that מחנה לויה could not have been the missing one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מדבר, a טמא מת was kept out only of מחנה שכינה, while a זב was kept out of both מחנה שכינה and מחנה לויה. Without מחנה לויה, both would be kept out of just one camp, and the difference between them would disappear. The plural word 'camps' in the פסוק requires a different boundary for each group.

keyTerms.meaning: People with a bodily discharge that makes them impure
People who became impure through contact with a dead body

phrases.english: It would turn out that zavim and those impure from a corpse
are sent outside one camp,
but the Torah said:
"that they not defile their camps"
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:3. The key is that 'camps' is plural.

phrases.english: Give a camp to this one and a camp to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצְאוּ זָבִין וּטְמֵאֵי מֵתִים מִשְׁתַּלְּחִין חוּץ לְמַחֲנֶה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an argument begun before this section about which camp was missing in שילה.
steps.raayaObject: מחנה לויה existed in שילה, so the missing camp would have to be מחנה ישראל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural 'מַחֲנֵיהֶם' in במדבר 5:3, read as 'a camp for this group and a camp for that group.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that מחנה לויה was the camp missing in שילה, based on the teaching that there were 'only two camps' there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without מחנה לויה, זבין and טמאי מתים would both be kept out of only one camp. But the plural 'מַחֲנֵיהֶם' (במדבר 5:3) requires a separate camp for each group.

steps.title: רבא: without the Israelite camp, a מצורע would not dwell alone
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that if מחנה ישראל was missing, זבין and מצורעים would be sent to the same place. The Torah says a מצורע must dwell alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: So what are you saying, that the Israelite camp did not exist? Then זבין and מצורעים would both be sent to one place! But the Torah said 'he shall dwell alone,' meaning no other impure person may live with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the other option, that מחנה ישראל was the missing camp. He shows this breaks a different Torah rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב is sent out beyond מחנה לויה, and a מצורע is sent out of all the camps. Without מחנה ישראל, the area outside מחנה לויה is already outside everything, so both would end up in the same place. The word 'בָּדָד' (alone) forbids putting a מצורע together with another impure person.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what are you saying? (pushes back on a claim)
The Israelite camp, the outermost camp

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Rather, what are you saying?
That the Israelite camp did not exist?!
Then it would turn out that zavim and lepers
are sent to one place,
but the Torah said: "He shall dwell alone"
meaning that no other impure person may dwell with him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אֶלָּא מַאי, מַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל לָא הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 1 implied that מחנה ישראל was the missing camp. רבא rejects that as well.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that מחנה ישראל was the camp missing in שילה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without מחנה ישראל, זבין and מצורעים would be in the same place, which breaks the rule of 'בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב.'

steps.title: All three camps existed; 'only two' is about giving refuge
steps.stepSummary: All three camps really existed in שילה. 'Only two camps' means that מחנה לויה did not give refuge to an accidental killer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really all three camps were there. And what does 'there were only two camps' mean? It is about giving refuge.
steps.whatsHappening: Since neither camp can be missing, the גמרא concludes all three existed. It reinterprets 'only two camps' as being about refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 1 and 2 showed that removing either מחנה לויה or מחנה ישראל breaks a Torah rule about the impure. So the 'two camps' statement cannot be about the physical layout of the camps. It means that in שילה, מחנה לויה did not work like an עיר מקלט for a רוצח בשוגג.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking in and protecting an accidental killer

steps.whatToRemember: In שילה all three camps existed. 'Only two camps' means only that מחנה לויה gave no refuge.

phrases.english: Rather, really all three were there;

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי לֹא הָיוּ אֶלָּא שְׁתֵּי מַחֲנוֹת –
phrases.english: and what does "there were only two camps" mean?
It is with regard to refuge.
phrases.notes: Refuge here means protecting someone who killed by accident, the way an עיר מקלט does.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem created by Steps 1 and 2, since neither camp can be removed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא's words as being about a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Only two camps' means one of the camps was physically missing in שילה.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three camps existed. Only the refuge function of מחנה לויה was missing.

steps.title: Did the Levite camp give refuge in the wilderness?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the answer implies that מחנה לויה did give refuge in the מדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that in the wilderness the Levite camp did give refuge?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an implication from the answer and asks about it. It is setting up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying that שילה lacked refuge in מחנה לויה suggests that in the מדבר it had refuge. The גמרא wants to know whether that is really true.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave refuge, took in and protected

phrases.english: Does this imply that in the wilderness
the Levite camp did give refuge?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דִּבְמִדְבָּר הֲוַאי קָלְטָה מַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from Step 3's answer about refuge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מחנה לויה served as a place of refuge for an accidental killer in the מדבר.

steps.title: Yes, the Levite camp gave refuge in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes: in the מדבר, the מחנה לויה did give refuge to an accidental killer. It proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. And so a ברייתא teaches: 'I will appoint for you a place' means even during your lifetime there will be a place of refuge, and 'a place' means your place. 'Where he may flee' teaches that they exiled killers even in the מדבר. Where did they go? To the מחנה לויה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4 with a clear 'yes.' It backs this up with a ברייתא that reads the פסוק as talking about refuge in the מדבר, in the Levite camp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads each part of the פסוק separately. 'For you' means during משה's own lifetime, so refuge already existed in the מדבר. 'A place' means 'your place,' the camp of the לויים. So the answer in step 3 is correct: only שילה lacked this, while the מדבר had it.

keyTerms.meaning: They send into exile (the accidental killer)

phrases.english: Yes;
and so it is taught in a ברייתא:
"And I will appoint for you a place":
during your lifetime; "a place" means your place;
phrases.notes: God is speaking to משה here. 'Your place' means the camp of the לויים.

phrases.english: "where he may flee."
This teaches that they would send killers into exile in the wilderness.
To where would they be exiled?
To the Levite camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and supports it with a ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did the מחנה לויה give refuge in the מדבר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The ברייתא learns from 'וְשַׂמְתִּי לְךָ מָקוֹם' that killers were exiled to the מחנה לויה in the מדבר.
steps.whatToRemember: In the מדבר, the מחנה לויה was the place of refuge for an accidental killer. In שילה it was not.

steps.title: A Levite who killed by accident
steps.stepSummary: From this, the חכמים learned that a לוי who killed by accident is exiled from one area to another, and if he went to another part of his own area, it still takes him in.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: a לוי who killed is exiled from district to district, and if he was exiled within his own district, his district takes him in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a הלכה that grows out of the ברייתא. It tells us what happens when a לוי, who already lives in a place of refuge, kills someone by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לויים lived inside the place of refuge, both in the מחנה לויה and later in the Levite cities. Even so, a לוי who kills by accident still has to go into exile. He moves to another district, and if he moves to another part of his own district, that also gives him refuge.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said (a rule learned from the source just quoted)

phrases.english: From here they said:
A Levite who killed (by accident)
is exiled from district to district,
and if he was exiled within his own district,
his district takes him in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a practical הלכה from the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי who killed by accident is exiled to another district. If he goes to another part of his own district, it gives him refuge.

steps.title: Which verse teaches this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק is the source for the rule about the לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a פסוק behind the rule it just stated. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in step 6 says that a place where the killer already lives can still take him in. That is surprising, so the גמרא wants a פסוק that shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (the source in the Torah)?

phrases.english: What is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the Torah source of the rule in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows that a place which already took in the killer can take him in again.

steps.title: The city that already took him in
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא brings the פסוק 'for in his city of refuge he shall dwell': a city that already took him in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא said: 'For in his city of refuge he shall dwell.' This means a city that already took him in.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא answers the question with a פסוק. The words 'his city of refuge' describe a city that already gave him refuge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls it 'his' city of refuge, a place that has already taken him in. This shows that a person who already lives in a place of refuge can be given refuge there again, which is the rule about the לוי.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rav Ika, said:
"For in his city of refuge he shall dwell":
a city that has already taken him in.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'כִּי בְעִיר מִקְלָטוֹ יֵשֵׁב' speaks of a city that already took him in.
steps.whatToRemember: A place where the killer already lives can still give him refuge. The source is 'כִּי בְעִיר מִקְלָטוֹ יֵשֵׁב.'

steps.title: גלגל: which offerings could go on a private altar, according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's words 'they came to גלגל.' A ברייתא says that a נדר or נדבה could be brought on a private במה, but a required offering could not. According to רבי מאיר, this includes a מנחה and the offerings of a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came to גלגל. The Rabbis taught: any offering that is a נדר or a נדבה was brought on a במה. Any offering that is not a נדר or a נדבה was not brought on a במה. A מנחה and the offerings of a נזיר were brought on a במה. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה about גלגל. It brings a ברייתא with רבי מאיר's view of which offerings an individual could bring on a private במה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's line is between offerings a person chooses to bring and offerings he is required to bring. Chosen offerings, נדר and נדבה, were allowed on a במה. Since nobody has to bring a מנחה or become a נזיר, those count as chosen offerings and were allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where בני ישראל camped after crossing the ירדן
An offering brought because of a vow, or given as a voluntary gift

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the issue is whether an offering is a קרבן at all. Every offering here is a real קרבן. The question is only which ones could be brought on a private במה.

phrases.english: They came to Gilgal.
The Rabbis taught:
Any offering brought because of a vow or as a voluntary gift
was brought on a private altar;
any offering that is not brought because of a vow or as a gift
was not brought on a private altar.
A meal offering and the offerings of a nazirite
were brought on a private altar.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the next line of the משנה, about גלגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, any נדר or נדבה, including a מנחה and the offerings of a נזיר, was brought on a private במה. Required offerings were not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main argument about what an individual could bring at a private במה during the times when במות were allowed.

steps.title: חכמים: only עולות and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and say that an individual brought only עולות and שלמים on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: an individual brought only עולות and שלמים, nothing else.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the other opinion. חכמים limit what an individual could bring on a private במה to עולות and שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allowed every chosen offering. חכמים allow only two kinds, עולות and שלמים. So according to חכמים, a מנחה and the offerings of a נזיר were not brought on a private במה.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
An individual did not bring (on a private altar)
anything except burnt offerings and peace offerings alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא קֵרְבוּ יָחִיד אֶלָּא עוֹלוֹת וּשְׁלָמִים בִּלְבָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, an individual brought only עולות and שלמים on a private במה. A מנחה and the offerings of a נזיר were not brought there.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: any נדר or נדבה, including a מנחה and a נזיר's offerings, could go on a private במה. חכמים: only עולות and שלמים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: גלגל took every offering the wilderness Tabernacle took
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that any offering, public or private, that was brought in the wilderness אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד was also brought in the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Any offering that the public or an individual brought in the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness was also brought in the Tent of Meeting in גלגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a three-way dispute. רבי יהודה goes first and says the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל worked just like the one in the wilderness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the main altar in גלגל lost any of its role once private במות became allowed. רבי יהודה says no. Even an individual's required offerings, like a חטאת, could still be brought there.

keyTerms.meaning: The Tent of Meeting, the Mishkan
The first place the Mishkan stood after entering ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Any offering that the public and the individual sacrifice
in the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
they sacrifice in the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about the period of גלגל and adds a new opinion about the main altar there.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All public and individual offerings of the wilderness were also brought at the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל.

steps.title: רבי יהודה explains the one difference: private altars
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה asks what the difference between the two periods was. He answers that private במות were forbidden in the wilderness but allowed in גלגל, though only for עולה and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the difference between the wilderness and גלגל? In the wilderness, private altars were not allowed. In גלגל, private altars were allowed. But on his private altar on his roof, a person could bring only burnt offerings and peace offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה asks his own question and answers it, to show what actually changed in גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main altar stayed the same. The only change was that a second option opened up: a private במה. That private option was limited to עולה and שלמים, so other offerings still had to go to the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד.

keyTerms.meaning: An altar; here, a private altar outside the Mishkan

steps.confusionAlert: There are two kinds of altar in גלגל: the big altar at the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד and the private במות. The limit to עולה and שלמים applies only to the private one.

phrases.english: And what is the difference between the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
and the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal?
At the time of the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
private altars were not permitted;
at the time of the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal
private altars were permitted.
But on his altar on top of his roof
he would not sacrifice upon it
anything but burnt offerings and peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַה בֵּין אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּמִּדְבָּר לְבֵין אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד שֶׁבַּגִּלְגָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהודה's opinion by showing what actually changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Private במות were allowed in גלגל, but only for עולה and שלמים.

steps.title: חכמים: individuals brought only עולה and שלמים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree that public offerings continued in גלגל. But they say an individual brought only עולה and שלמים, both at the main altar and on a private במה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: Any offering the public brought in the wilderness אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד was brought in the אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד in גלגל. But in both places, an individual brought only עולה and שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי יהודה about individuals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the main altar still took an individual's required offerings. The חכמים take out the word 'individual' from the first rule. They say an individual's required offerings were not brought at all in that period, even at the big altar.

keyTerms.meaning: Here and here; in both places

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
Any offering that the public sacrifices
in the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness
they sacrifice in the Tent of Meeting in Gilgal;
and here and here, an individual did not sacrifice
phrases.notes: 'Here and here' means both the big altar in גלגל and a private altar.

phrases.english: anything except burnt offerings and peace offerings alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה about an individual's offerings at the main altar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גלגל, an individual brought only עולה and שלמים, both at the main altar and on a private במה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: even the public brought only limited offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון narrows things further. Even the public did not bring everything in גלגל, only פסחים, and his list continues.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even the public sacrificed only Paschal offerings...
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion begins. רבי שמעון limits even the public's offerings in גלגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים limited only individuals. רבי שמעון also cuts down the public offerings. The list of what the public did bring continues in the next part of the text.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views on גלגל: רבי יהודה (everything continued at the main altar), the חכמים (individuals only עולה and שלמים), and רבי שמעון (even the public was limited).

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even the public did not sacrifice
anything but Paschal offerings

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף צִבּוּר לֹא הִקְרִיבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than the חכמים by limiting public offerings too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In גלגל, even the public brought only a limited set of offerings, beginning with פסחים.
